name: Garland v. Aleman Gonzalez
summary: The Supreme Court held that §1252(f)(1) prohibits lower federal courts from entering injunctions that restrain the operation of immigration removal statutes, though it left open questions about other forms of relief such as declaratory judgments.
significance: This case directly interpreted the scope of 8 U.S.C. §1252(f)(1), holding that the provision strips lower courts of jurisdiction to issue class-wide injunctions against the operation of removal statutes.
